QUOTE: "It then calls `client.createPost` again. On success it writes the server post and updates the last-post time for the channel... On failure, the same error handling applies: the three "removal" errors delete the post, and everything else sets `failed: true` again."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says retryFailedPost calls createPost once more and, on failure, either removes the post for the same three errors or marks it failed again. Part 1 says nothing in `createPost` loops or reschedules, and the retry just re-runs that send, so the no-loop point is covered.
